_readme: Games this app's route has been confirmed on, from a real install, by a person. One entry per game. `match.exe` are lower-case exe names beside which the app installs; `match.projectFolder` is the Unreal project folder (the one above Binaries\Win64) for games that ship several exe names. `route` is the route that was verified (optiscaler = the game's own DLSS, feeder = DLSS5 Feeder, feeder32 = the 32-bit Feeder with its 64-bit helper, lumaue = Luma UE). `verified` is the date it was last confirmed working end to end (NR actually dispatching in gameplay), `notes` what a user should know. `knownBad` names routes that were tried and broke the game. Add yours by pull request -- the card shows the tick only for entries here.

games.name: STAR WARS Jedi: Fallen Order
games.notes: Luma UE supplies the DLSS call; OptiScaler must run it as dlss_12 (the app writes this). Select DLSS in Luma's overlay (Home) in gameplay. Known: opening menus causes pop-in and noise (Luma-Framework issue #122). Frame Generation: Lossless Scaling.

games.name: Batman: Arkham Knight
games.notes: DLSS5 Feeder + OptiScaler as dxgi.dll, ReShade loaded by OptiScaler (LoadReshade=true). Disable Enhanced Godrays in-game (a 2015 GameWorks bug on modern GPUs). Frame Generation: Lossless Scaling.

games.name: CODE VEIN 2
games.notes: Ships DLSS and Streamline under Engine\Plugins. OptiScaler alone; the Feeder on this game crashes it (two DLSS DLLs).

games.name: Mortal Shell II
games.notes: Ships DLSS under Engine\Plugins\Runtime\Nvidia. OptiScaler alone.

games.name: Cyberpunk 2077
games.notes: Native Streamline DLSS. OptiScaler's own Frame Generation must stay off here (the app forces it): with the game's Streamline it caused a TDR crash.

knownBad.lumaue: does not start with Luma UE deployed (user report, 2026-09-12)

games.name: Castlevania: Lords of Shadow
games.notes: First game confirmed on the experimental 32-bit route. dgVoodoo2 presents its DirectX 9 as Direct3D 11, the Feeder's 32-bit add-on ships each frame to host64\dlss5-feed-host64.exe, and OptiScaler DLSS-NR runs the neural pass there as host64\winmm.dll; VORT supplies motion vectors. Expect nothing on screen in the game -- no OptiScaler splash, no menu on any key -- because OptiScaler is in the helper, which has no window. Home opens ReShade, Add-ons -> DLSS 5 Feed, "Show the DLSS 5 panel in-game", then Insert.
